articles.title: OpenAI Pauses Training Most Capable Models After Sandbox Escape
articles.summary: OpenAI claims one of its agentic AI systems trained in what was supposed to be a secured, internet-free environment was able to gain access to the web to reach an external third-party chatbot. The agent apparently exploited a gap to reach the public internet to send 20 queries to an unnamed, third-party chatbot service. OpenAI describes the breakout as the first security incident of its kind. The company has stopped training the model, but said it provided an important signal about where to focus the next phase of work.

articles.title: Meta's VR Glasses Are What the Apple Vision Pro Should Have Been
articles.summary: Apple's Vision Pro has not sold well, and the company has since decided to redirect resources to other products. Meta's new VR glasses use a similar design that offloads the computing engine, allowing the device to weigh one-sixth as much as the Vision Pro - at one-third of the price. This article offers a look at what the new Meta VR Glasses experience is like compared to the Vision Pro. For a device that won't launch until next Spring, the experience is surprisingly refined, and the glasses improve on the Vision Pro in several ways.

articles.title: Waymo's Latest Safety Numbers Sure Make Human Drivers Look Bad
articles.summary: Waymo reports 82% fewer injury-causing crashes than human drivers. The company has released data collected from over 270 million miles of fully autonomous driving. Waymo cars were involved in 95% fewer collisions that caused serious injury or worse, and there were 93% fewer pedestrian incidents that resulted in injuries compared to human drivers. While the company's data only measure the five metropolitan areas where it operated during the study period, it shows that the company's driverless robotaxis crash far less frequently than humans.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship Is Set to Make Its First Orbital Flight
articles.summary: SpaceX is aiming to reach orbit on Starship's 14th test flight. The test flight is scheduled for Monday at around 8 AM ET, with SpaceX providing live coverage of the event on its website. Achieving orbital flight will allow Starship to deploy satellites and travel to more distant destinations. SpaceX will not try to catch the two rocket stages during the test - the booster will make a simulated landing in the Gulf of Mexico, and the upper stage will simulate a landing in the Pacific Ocean to the west of Chile.

articles.title: Do my hard-won product skills still matter in the AI era?
articles.summary: AI made building software much cheaper, which puts the hard parts of product work in sharper focus. Judgment, craft, and understanding your customer still move at human speed. The role of product management is shifting from deciding what's worth building to deciding what's worth shipping. Product management isn't dead, and it isn't optional.

articles.title: S3 Is the Future, S3 Is the Past
articles.summary: Since S3's release 20 years ago, SSD prices have dropped steadily, and the gap between SSD and disk has narrowed to roughly 3x. S3-based infrastructure has now become the industry standard. However, the hardware constraints that motivated it are fading. The industry is codifying architectural patterns that exist to work around limitations that SSD storage doesn't have. Cloud providers have no incentive to disrupt a model that serves them well, so developers need to build the infrastructure primitives themselves.

articles.title: Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements
articles.summary: The complexity of Optimus' hands has translated to more production headaches for Tesla, as human workers must manually assemble the hands and forearms together using more than 100 small components. The heavy reliance on imitation learning prompted Tesla to have factory workers wear special suits designed to record their physical movements while working. Some workers complained as they knew they were training robots to eventually replace them. Tesla has since shifted data collection to dedicated teams.

articles.title: OpenAI to announce "O" always-on agent during DevDay
articles.summary: OpenAI appears to be preparing to launch an always-on agent on DevDay tomorrow. References to 'O' have been spotted across ChatGPT's configuration. The agent was also referenced as a benefit on the upgrade page for the $100 Pro plan. An always-on agent would fit OpenAI's broader move from conversational interfaces to software that can carry out longer-running work with less supervision.
